title: Steps of Service
summary: The Pelagos service standard from greeting to farewell: the timing benchmarks, the steps of service and how to upsell naturally.
body:
## 1. PURPOSE

This SOP sets clear, consistent service standards so that every guest receives efficient, attentive and memorable service. It also aims to grow revenue through professional, natural upselling while keeping the guest experience exceptional.

## 2. SCOPE AND RESPONSIBILITY

- **Primary responsibility:** Duty Manager.
- **Applies to:** all front of house staff, including waitrons, runners, deli assistants and bartenders.

## 3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

### 3.1 Front of house staff

- Greet and seat guests promptly and professionally.
- Take accurate orders within the times in section 4.
- Guide guests through the menu using confident, suggestive selling.
- Monitor table satisfaction and do quality checks.
- Offer refills and additional items throughout service.
- Handle basic complaints and escalate to the Duty Manager when needed (see PEL-SOP-002).
- Present the bill and process payment efficiently.
- Give every table a warm, professional farewell.

### 3.2 Duty Manager

- Do daily floor and hygiene inspections.
- Monitor service flow and guest satisfaction.
- Support an upselling culture and staff performance.
- Deal with guest complaints promptly and professionally.
- Coach staff on service standards and sales techniques.

## 4. SERVICE TIMING BENCHMARKS

| **Stage**                   | **Target time**                                                            |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Guests acknowledged**     | Within 30 seconds of arrival (a smile and “I’ll be right with you” counts) |
| **Guests greeted**          | Within 1 minute of arrival                                                 |
| **Guests seated**           | Immediately on arrival, or as soon as the table is ready                   |
| **Drinks order taken**      | Within 2 minutes of seating                                                |
| **Drinks delivered**        | Within 3 to 5 minutes of the order                                         |
| **Starter order taken**     | Within 5 to 8 minutes of seating                                           |
| **Starters delivered**      | Within 10 to 12 minutes of the order                                       |
| **Main course order taken** | With the starter order, or shortly after starters are served               |
| **Main courses delivered**  | Within 15 to 20 minutes after starter plates are cleared                   |
| **Quality check**           | Within two bites or two minutes of each course arriving                    |
| **Payment processed**       | Within 2 minutes of the guest asking for the bill                          |

## 5. STEPS OF SERVICE

### 5.1 Greeting and seating (within 1 minute)

**Objective:** make a strong first impression and build rapport.

- Acknowledge every guest within 30 seconds, even if you are busy (the 30-Second Rule).
- Greet guests warmly with eye contact and a genuine smile.
- Introduce yourself confidently.
- Hand out menus immediately.

> **Say:** *“Welcome to Pelagos, my name is [Name], and I’ll be taking care of you today.”*

**Upsell opportunity:** mention the specials early.

> **Say:** *“We have a fresh seafood special today that I highly recommend.”*

### 5.2 Drinks order and water service (within 2 minutes)

**Objective:** start service quickly and make the first upsell.

- Offer water immediately.
- Recommend specific drinks instead of asking open-ended questions.
- Offer premium upgrades (large instead of small, double shots, premium brands).
- Deliver drinks promptly and confirm the guest is happy.

> **Say:** *“Can I start you with one of our signature cocktails or a glass of Sauvignon Blanc?”*

### 5.3 Starter order and menu guidance (within 5 to 8 minutes)

**Objective:** guide the guest experience and increase the spend per table.

- Answer menu questions confidently.
- Ask about allergies and dietary requirements before taking the order, and tell the kitchen clearly.
- Suggest starters and sharing plates.
- Take the starter order first, then ask whether the table is ready to order mains or needs more time.

> **Say:** *“Our calamari is very popular and perfect for sharing while you decide on mains.”*

### 5.4 Main course order

**Objective:** make sure the order is accurate and add value for each guest. Take the main course order with the starter order, or shortly after the starters are served.

- Take main course orders clearly and confidently.
- Repeat the full order back to the table for accuracy, including any allergies and changes.
- Suggest add-ons, sides or upgrades.
- Recommend a wine to go with the main course.
- Present, open and pour the wine before the food arrives (see PEL-MAN-003 Wine Theory and Service Manual).

> **Say:** *“Would you like to add a side of grilled prawns to your steak?”*
>
> **Say:** *“That dish pairs beautifully with our house red. Would you like a glass or a bottle?”*

### 5.5 Quality check (two bites or two minutes)

**Objective:** confirm satisfaction and fix any problem quickly.

- Check back within two bites or two minutes of the food arriving.
- Ask specific questions rather than “is everything okay?”.
- Refill drinks before they drop below one-third full.
- If there is a problem, follow PEL-SOP-002 Handling Complaints and Food Returns.

> **Say:** *“Is your steak cooked the way you like it?”*

### 5.6 Table maintenance (continuous)

**Objective:** keep the table clean and comfortable.

- Clear used plates, glasses and clutter promptly and quietly.
- Keep the table neat at all times.
- Refold napkins when guests leave the table.
- Watch for cues (empty glasses, finished sharing plates) and suggest the next item.

### 5.7 Dessert, coffee and after-dinner drinks

**Objective:** maximise final sales and end on a high note.

- Clear the table before presenting the dessert menu.
- Suggest desserts with a pairing.
- Offer coffee, liqueurs and after-dinner drinks.

> **Say:** *“Our house-made Portokalopita goes perfectly with a cappuccino or a dessert wine.”*

### 5.8 The bill and farewell

**Objective:** a smooth, memorable departure.

- Present the bill only when the guest asks for it or is clearly finished.
- Ask whether the guest is a Maxiclub member before the bill is closed, and follow PEL-MAN-002 Maxiclub POS User Guide.
- Process payment within 2 minutes, by card on the TABBS machine. Pelagos is cashless: we never accept cash from a guest. If a guest offers cash, politely explain this and offer to take payment by card.
- Thank guests sincerely and invite them back.

> **Say:** *“Thank you for joining us today, [Name if known]. We look forward to welcoming you again soon.”*

## 6. UPSELLING PRINCIPLES

- Be natural, not pushy.
- Always recommend a specific item rather than asking a general question.
- Use descriptive language.
- Focus on improving the guest’s experience.
- Read the table and adjust your approach.
- Every interaction is a chance to add value.

## 7. RELATED DOCUMENTS

- PEL-MAN-004 FOH Training Manual (training for these steps)
- PEL-SOP-002 Handling Complaints and Food Returns
- PEL-SOP-003 Dineplan Reservations
- PEL-MAN-002 Maxiclub POS User Guide
- PEL-MAN-003 Wine Theory and Service Manual
- PEL-POL-001 Staff Handbook (section 8, Service standards)
